source_review.notes: Checked current official Apache Spark task-failure/speculation and RDD documentation; Apache Hadoop JobConf, TaskAttemptContext, and MapReduce tutorial; Apache Flink task recovery, restart/backoff, batch progress recovery, and high availability; Apache Beam execution model; and the original MapReduce and Tail at Scale publications. All twelve URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date. Sources support attempt limits, speculation controls, failover scope, backoff strategies, bundle/region reprocessing, retained progress, and tail-latency claims.

evidence: Reviewed logical task T, attempts A_i, generation g, capped exponential delays, cohort median/threshold, elapsed/progress/remaining estimates, candidate artifacts, and commit token.
Checked task, attempt, retry, speculation, failover scope, winner, cancellation, and committed logical output remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Attempt count and retry count are not conflated; concrete engine semantics must define whether the initial attempt is included.

evidence: Executed retry-and-speculation-policy with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced capped delays 2, 4, and 8.
Recomputed peer median 10, threshold 15, partition-7 remaining estimate 24, partition-9 estimate about 2.2, and speculation of partition-7 only.
Confirmed attempt-1 finish 26 beats attempt-0 finish 40 while both attempts are charged and one stable logical commit token is used.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The linear progress estimate is explicitly labeled as a fallible policy model rather than true remaining duration.

evidence: Verified d_i=min(cap,base*factor^(i-1)) and reviewed fixed, exponential, capped, jittered, elapsed, attempt, failure-rate, and work budgets.
Checked retry safety requires equivalent candidates under pinned inputs/context plus atomic publication of at most one winner.
Reviewed cohort comparison, minimum evidence, estimated benefit, duplicate cost, and failure-domain diversity for speculation.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Publication uniqueness does not imply external-effect uniqueness without an idempotent, transactional, outbox, or reconciliation protocol.

evidence: Reviewed zero retries, attempts versus retries, cap/deadline exhaustion, scheduler restart, correlated dependency outage, synchronized storms, stale budgets, worker/rack faults, and quarantines.
Reviewed poison records, deterministic code, schema/input drift, memory/resource failures, policy denial, expired credentials, cancellation, preemption, and ambiguous remote effects.
Reviewed incomparable partitions, nonlinear progress, hot keys, saturated shared bottlenecks, scarce accelerators, late losers, stale generation, commit races, checksum failure, and cleanup retry.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Transient recovery, deterministic defect handling, skew remediation, and external-effect reconciliation are separate responses.

evidence: Traced job/plan/stage/partition/input task identity through unique attempts, generations, workers, candidates, validation, commit winner, cancellation, and cleanup.
Checked immutable source/schema/code/configuration/security context and stable randomness/clock policy across recomputation.
Checked retries/speculation consume quota/fair share/rate limits, stale attempts cannot publish, and effects remain transactionally or idempotently reconciled.
invariant_checking.notes: Failover scope follows valid materialization/state boundaries and records every invalidated task.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from identity/classification through failover scope, budgets, attempt isolation, atomic commit, effect handling, cohorts, duplicate bounds, and adversarial evaluation.

Checked counterexamples for retry-as-repair, attempt/retry confusion, incident erasure by success, speculation-as-timeout, slowest-as-defective, independent duplicates, winner-only accounting, last-writer-wins, cancellation fencing, timeless idempotency, and unlimited retries.
Reviewed conditional retry-correctness proof and empirical net-benefit burden for speculation.
proof_review.notes: Straggler detection identifies candidates under uncertainty and never proves worker fault or expected benefit by itself.

evidence: Audited uses of retryable, transient, deterministic, immutable, equivalent, atomic, authoritative, idempotent, transactional, stale, isolated, safe, straggler, and beneficial.
Confirmed the executable fixture is labeled as a local policy arithmetic model rather than a production detector, failure simulator, or commit service.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Engine-specific retry defaults and failover behaviors are sourced rather than generalized.

evidence: Reviewed attempt distribution, retry CPU/bytes/cost, recovery, speculation launch/win, critical-path savings, duplicate work, loser lifetime, bottleneck load, task/stage/job tails, output equivalence, and cohort outcomes.
Confirmed no universal attempt count, delay, jitter, detector multiplier, progress model, speculative cap, win-rate target, legal approval, or external-review claim is made.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production tuning requires exact engine/policy, workload cohorts, data/resource topology, dependencies, effects, and failure distributions.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed task/attempt identity, failure taxonomy and scope, backoff/budgets, deterministic recomputation, candidate commit, external effects, straggler estimation, speculative value, skew, cancellation, amplification, observability, security, and governance as one recovery model.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed persistent attempt generations/budgets, health-aware placement, pinned execution inputs, atomic manifests, stale fencing, cleanup, idempotency/reconciliation, cohort features, speculative caps, failure injection, bottleneck/fairness metrics, sensitive artifacts, cohort harm, appeal, and named review. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from identity and failure classification through retry mechanics, commit/effects, speculation/skew, amplification, evidence, and governance; ten examples and five complete answers cover arithmetic, classification, protocol, experiments, and regulated use.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Spark, Hadoop, Flink, or Beam maintainer, distributed-systems researcher, tail-latency/statistics specialist, scheduler/performance engineer, database/payment-effects expert, security auditor, privacy/legal/records authority, affected-community reviewer, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
